issues.failure_explanation: The mollifier ζ lives on R×R^d and the same d-dimensional shift e is applied simultaneously to x, y and z, so the convolution smooths only along the diagonal direction (1,1,1) in R^{3d}. For a Lipschitz function such as v(t,x,y,z)=|x−y| one gets v^ε=|x−y| exactly, which is not C^1. Hence the claim v^ε∈C_b^∞ and the bounds ‖∂_t^i D^j v^ε‖≤2CK_ζ ε^{1−2i−j} are false in general. The proof of Theorem main theorem substitutes u^ε and u_h^ε into Lemma consistency (which requires C_b^∞ with bounded derivatives of all orders in x,y,z separately) and uses (u_mollifer), (uh_mollifer), so as written the derivation of E_1, E_2 rests on an invalid premise.

failure_location.quote: v^{\varepsilon}(t,x,y,z) := (v \ast \zeta_{\varepsilon})(t,x,y,z) := \int_{-\varepsilon^{2}}^{0} \int_{|e| < \varepsilon} v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e) \, \zeta_{\varepsilon}(\tau, e) \, de \, d\tau

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the mollifier by one on R×R^{3d} with independent shifts (e_1,e_2,e_3) for (x,y,z) (scaling ε^{-(2+3d)}); the standard estimates and the supersolution/Jensen arguments then hold verbatim with adjusted K_ζ.
issues.overall_effect: The regularization step underpinning both error bounds in Theorem main theorem, and hence all convergence-rate results, is not established as written.
issues.title: Diagonal mollification (same shift e in x, y, z) does not regularize; smoothness and derivative bounds of u^ε, u_h^ε unfounded
issues.why_classification: A local, standard correction of the regularization construction restores every claim, rate and constant structure without new arguments.

issues.failure_explanation: u_h is piecewise constant in t with jumps of size up to C_0 h^{1/2} at grid points, so Lemma uh_regularity (ii) necessarily carries the extra h^{1/2}; property (C1) as stated (pure 1/2-Hölder in t with constant C_0 independent of h) is false. Consequently the mollification error ‖u_h − u_h^ε‖ is only bounded by C(ε + h^{1/2}) (e.g. t just before a grid point with ε^2 straddling the jump), not by 2C_0 ε as asserted in (uh_mollifer) — inconsistent with the derivative bound in the same display that does carry (ε+h^{1/2}). The step showing underline{u}(h) ≤ ū(h) in the lower-bound proof uses the wrong bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State (C1) with the additional h^{1/2}, use ‖u_h − u_h^ε‖ ≤ C_0(2ε + h^{1/2}) (or similar), and enlarge the h^{1/2} coefficient in underline{u} and in the lower bound accordingly (e.g. 3C_0 h^{1/2}); adjust downstream constants.
issues.overall_effect: The constant in the lower bound (i) of Theorem main theorem and in the derived CLT bounds is not justified as stated; the exponent/rate is unaffected.
issues.title: h^{1/2} term in time regularity of u_h dropped in (C1) and in ‖u_h − u_h^ε‖ ≤ 2C_0 ε
issues.why_classification: Only constants change; a short local correction preserves every rate and guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption (vi) yields, for each fixed φ∈C_b^3(R^d), a function l̂_φ, uniform only in the shift z. In the proof, φ = u^ε(t,x,y,·) varies with (t,x,y), so l̂_{u^ε(t,x,y,z+·)}(h) is a family of functions and E_2(ε,h) (likewise E_1) is not a function of (ε,h). Lemma comparison requires sup_{[h,1]×R^{3d}}(f_1−f_2)^+, i.e. sup_{t,x,y} l̂_{u^ε(t,x,y,·)}(h), whose finiteness (and decay in h) is not guaranteed by Assumption (vi). The same gap affects the lower bound where ū = u_h^ε + E_1(t−h) must be a supersolution at all points.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen Assumption (vi) so that l̂ depends on φ only via bounds on its derivatives up to order 3 (as in Section 4), and define E_i with the corresponding uniform quantity; the proofs then go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem main theorem's bounds are not well defined/justified under Assumption (vi) as stated; the examples are unaffected because there l̂_φ depends on φ only through ‖Dφ‖,‖D²φ‖.
issues.title: E_1, E_2 depend on (t,x,y,z) through l̂_{u^ε(t,x,y,z+·)}(h); uniform bound needed by the comparison lemma is not provided by Assumption (vi)
issues.why_classification: A standard local strengthening of the hypothesis, already satisfied by the examples, closes the gap without altering results or rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate bounds |Δ_xω|^{3/2} by min(2‖D_xω‖, ‖D²_{xz}ω‖h^{1/α}|Z|)^{3/2} ≤ (2‖D_xω‖)^{3/2−δ}(‖D²_{xz}ω‖h^{1/α}|Z|)^δ, which is valid only when 0 ≤ δ ≤ 3/2. For α ∈ (3/2,2), Assumption (v) permits δ ∈ (3/2, α); then 3/2−δ < 0 and the inequality fails (min^{3/2−δ} ≥ a^{3/2−δ}). The resulting exponent (3−2δ)/3 < 0 on ‖D_xω‖ also makes the later step ‖D_x u^ε‖^{(3−2δ)/3}‖D²_{xz}u^ε‖^{2δ/3} ≤ 2C_0K_ζ ε^{−2δ/3} invalid (an upper bound on ‖D_x u^ε‖ cannot bound a negative power). Since (4δ−3α)/(2α(2δ+3)) is increasing in δ, the rate claimed in Theorems main theorem ex1 / ex1 CLT for δ > 3/2 exceeds what the method yields (any admissible Hölder split gives at best the δ = 3/2 value (2−α)/(4α)). Remark remark_delta also omits this constraint.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Assumption (v) to δ ∈ (¾α ∨ 1, α ∧ 3/2] (or replace δ by δ∧3/2 in all exponents), and restate Γ accordingly; for δ ≥ 3/2 the rate contribution becomes (2−α)/(4α).
issues.overall_effect: Lemma consistency and the definitions of E_1, E_2 are unproven for δ ∈ (3/2, α); the advertised rate Γ(α,δ,q_0) is unsupported in that regime (α > 3/2 with δ > 3/2), and the stated dependence on δ overstates the achievable exponent.
issues.title: Interpolation in R_21 requires δ ≤ q_1 = 3/2, but Assumption (v) allows δ up to α > 3/2; consistency bound and rate unsupported for δ > 3/2
issues.why_classification: A contained correction of the admissible range restores validity, but it necessarily weakens the stated convergence exponent in the regime α > 3/2, δ > 3/2, so mathematical content is lost while a comparable result survives.
